---
title: Combine calibrated images
description: Combine CCDData inputs and choose calibration and rejection explicitly.
---

Use `imcombine` for a FITS-aware combination of exposures. This example uses
three small `CCDData` images so the result can be checked directly.

## 1. Prepare images with matching units

```{python}
import numpy as np
from astropy.nddata import CCDData

from astroimred.imutil.imcombine import imcombine

frames = [
    CCDData(np.full((16, 16), level, dtype="float32"), unit="adu")
    for level in (100, 102, 104)
]
```

For observed images, load the frames with `air.load_ccd` after applying the
calibration required by the instrument. Combination does not infer which bias,
dark, or flat frames belong to an observation.

## 2. Combine and verify the result

```{python}
combined = imcombine(frames, combine="average")
np.testing.assert_allclose(combined.data, 102.0)
combined.shape, float(combined.data.mean())
```

Use `combine="median"` when the sample median is the desired statistic.
Choose rejection, zero/scale corrections, and weights for the observation;
they can change the scientific meaning of the output.

## 3. Select the next operation

| Need | Entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Bias, dark, and flat correction | [`ccdred`](../api/reduction.preproc.ccdred.qmd) |
| Group exposures by header fields | [`group_combine`](../api/imutil.imcombine.group_combine.qmd) |
| Arithmetic between images | [`imarith`](../api/imutil.imarith.imarith.qmd) |
| Detailed normalization and rejection controls | [`imcombine`](../api/imutil.imcombine.imcombine.qmd) |

`output_std` describes sample/clipping spread. It is not a propagated
uncertainty image; explicit input-uncertainty extension requests are currently
unsupported. Read the API's return values before using diagnostics downstream.
